reason: Carbon dioxide dissolving in rain is a plausible first step toward water that can weather basalt.
expectation: The water will take up carbon dioxide, making it more capable of dissolving rock.

effect: The rain is now mildly acidic, making it a plausible agent for weathering the basalt.
reaction: The result matches my expectation and clarifies that the effect is selective, not instant.
reason: Acidic rain can react with minerals in the young basaltic crust.
expectation: The rain will weather the basalt and release some dissolved material.

effect: The acidic rain altered basalt and released dissolved constituents; the next step is to move them toward the sea.
reaction: The distinction between chemical weathering and biological soil is useful.
reason: Runoff can carry material released from the weathering basalt toward the basin.
expectation: The runoff will carry dissolved rock constituents toward the sea.

effect: The runoff now carries dissolved ions, ready to deliver them to the sea.
reaction: It is useful to see how clear-looking water can carry material from rock.
reason: The runoff can deliver its dissolved constituents to the accumulating sea.
expectation: The dissolved material will enter the sea.

effect: The dissolved constituents have entered the sea, completing the first goal; sediment remains.
reaction: The distinction between early sea chemistry and modern seawater is useful.
reason: The altered basalt is a plausible source of sediment, but its next available use is not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection may reveal how the altered rock produces material that can settle.

alternatives.reason: Runoff might deposit sediment in sheltered water, but I do not yet know whether it carries particles.

effect: The inspection automatically loosened fine solid particles from the altered basalt, providing material for the sediment goal.
reaction: The contrast between solid particles and dissolved ions is useful.
reason: Runoff can transport the newly loosened particles toward the sea.
expectation: The runoff will carry the fine particles toward the basin.

effect: The runoff now carries suspended solid particles toward the coast, ready to settle.
reaction: The distinction between cloudy sediment and dissolved material is clear.
reason: Sheltered water should slow the flow enough for fine particles to settle.
expectation: The suspended particles will settle as fine sediment.

effect: The suspended particles settled in sheltered water, completing the sediment goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the solid-particle route end in a sediment bed, distinct from the dissolved load.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following weathered basalt into both dissolved ions and solid sediment was most worthwhile: it showed two different ways water transports rock-derived material.

leastWorthwhile.text: Delivering the dissolved material to the sea was a predictable final step, though it completed the process clearly.

surprise.text: Inspecting the altered basalt automatically combined it with rain and revealed that weathering also produces solid particles, not just dissolved ions.

arbitrary.text: No action felt notably arbitrary; the inspection was useful because the sediment route was not yet clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the paired transport routes made the natural processes understandable, and I would be curious to see what happens to the sediment next.
